transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-04
Time: 14:00 - 15:00 UTC
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Derek (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM); Priya (Novaleap VP Eng), Jonah (Head of MLOps), Aisha (Procurement), Marco (SRE)

Summary (auto): High-level renewal check-in. Discussed optional commitment uplift, multi-region (EU + APAC) activation, latency targets for new workload, and security/KMS prerequisites. Agreed next steps for benchmark and draft amendment.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call, say your name and role if you can.
[00:08] Priya: Hi yes Priya Nambiar, VP Engineering at Novaleap.
[00:11] Jonah: Jonah Ruiz, MLOps lead.
[00:14] Aisha: Aisha Khan from procurement.
[00:16] Marco: Marco Li, SRE.
[00:18] Maya: Great. From Redwood we've got Derek SE, Lena CSM. We'll run through current usage, renewal options and then dig into region/provisioning details.

[00:30] Derek: Quick context — we saw your token consumption growth Q3->Q4, about +34% month over month on inference. You're starting to push more synchronous traffic and the p95 latency on hosted edge has crept. So options are straightforward: reserve Dedicated pool for steady throughput, or keep Hosted and add burst + routing to EU region.

[00:54] Jonah: Okay, can you expand on 'crept'? Our p95's gone up from ~120ms to mid 160's on longer prompts under concurrent load. That's been the pain for product.
[01:10] Derek: Yeah, thanks. The write-up in the dashboard shows under 800-1k concurrent qps the KV cache misses and batching backpressure cause p95 fluctuations. We can improve by Dedicated with higher guaranteed GPUs and continuous batching tuned per model, or through optimizations like prefix-KV caching and smaller batch-size, but that trades off cost.

[01:40] Maya: Just to be clear on business ask — we heard at renewal you wanted predictability and lower unit cost, plus EU residency. Correct?
[01:47] Priya: Correct. Predictable spend and sub-150ms p95 for search flows. Also, we have privacy rules in EU that may force residency for PHI-related items.

[02:02] Aisha: Procurement also needs clarity on billing cadence and PO terms — can't have open-ended burst without a committed band.

[02:12] Lena: Noted. We have two proposal tracks: 1) 12-month amendment adding Dedicated capacity pool sized to your 95th-percentile sustained load with burst credits for spikes; 2) 6-month pilot for EU private deployment (VPC + KMS) + Dedicated for US region. Each has different pricing & SLAs.

[02:36] Marco: For the EU private pilot — do you offer customer-managed KMS? And will audit logs be shipped to our Splunk?
[02:44] Derek: Yes to customer-managed KMS (we integrate with common KMS/HSM providers). Audit logs are available via secure export; we support Splunk/ELK ingestion endpoints. There are some retention tier options that affect cost.

[03:02] Priya: One thing — our compliance team will ask for SOC2 type II evidence and a network diagram. Can you forward that?
[03:08] Maya: Absolutely. We'll send the SOC2 report and a high-level private deployment diagram after the call.

[03:17] Priya: Thanks. On latency: is Dedicated the only way to get stable sub-150ms p95?
[03:25] Derek: Not the only way, but the most reliable. Hosted can achieve it for most cases if we pin to smaller model variants, use KV caching aggressively, and enable region routing to EU for EU users. But under sustained concurrent load, Dedicated with a reserved GPU pool gives you consistent latencies and predictable unit economics. And we can configure the serving runtime with quantization/compiled kernels to optimize further.

[03:52] Jonah: Can you quantify the cost delta? A ballpark percent uplift for Dedicated vs hosted with burst credits?
[03:58] Maya: Roughly, Dedicated is ~45-60% higher in base commit cost but reduces per-token unit cost by ~20-40% due to reserved capacity, batching, and locality. The exact depends on model mix and batch patterns. We'll run a breakdown for your current workload.

[04:17] Marco: On the technical side — how do rollouts work for model updates? We don't want a new model to regress latency/quality.
[04:24] Derek: We support canary rollouts and A/B testing at route level. There's automatic fallback to previous model variant on error or quality regression thresholds. Also Redwood Optimize can evaluate prompt sets and run regression alerts.

[04:40] Priya: For the EU requirement — do you have fully private control plane option or just tenant VPC? The legal team is strict about data egress.
[04:49] Maya: We offer both: VPC-hosted private deployment with Redwood-managed control plane in a customer VPC, and an on-prem package for fully air-gapped setups. Most customers start with VPC+KMS and move to on-prem only if required.

[05:05] Aisha: Timeline wise — if we sign an amendment in mid-December, when could EU region be live?
[05:12] Lena: Typical timelines: VPC private onboarding 6-8 weeks after PO (including network setup and KMS key exchange). If you want a narrow pilot in one EU region only, we can compress to 4-6 weeks with prioritization.

[05:25] Jonah: We also want to run a latency benchmark: 1k qps sustained 5 minute windows with mixed short & long prompts. Can Redwood run that or do we run it?
[05:34] Derek: We can run it on our staging with your prompt set (you provide prompts and auth). We'll produce p50/p95/p99, token counts, and a KV cache hit/miss breakdown. Ideally we'll mirror your productionish traffic shape.

[05:47] Priya: OK we'll share a sanitized prompt set by Monday. There's some PHI concern so we'll sanitize and include examples.

[05:55] Maya: Great. On pricing shapes — for 12-month commit we can propose tiered dedicated units: base commit for 95th percentile sustained, plus burst credits that are metered. The amendment can include an early exit clause with a small termination fee if needed.

[06:12] Marco: What about autoscaling behavior? If dedicated pool is saturated, do you route to hosted fallback?
[06:19] Derek: Yes, smart routing can failover to hosted region variants with lower SLAs. There are policies at customer route level: strict (no fallback), permissive (fallback allowed), and hybrid (fallback for non-PHI traffic). You can configure per-route.

[06:36] Priya: For PHI we need strict no-fallback to hosted. Can that be enforced by route?
[06:41] Derek: Yes we can set route-level policy to strict. We'll document the routing policy and the fallback behavior in the SOW.

[06:50] Aisha: Procurement question — if price is higher for Dedicated, can we structure a staggered PO (quarterly top-ups) tied to usage?
[06:58] Maya: Yes, we can do staged PO or tiered commit where you start with smaller baseline and trigger scheduled top-ups or automated scale windows. We'll include a few suggested cadence options in the price sheet.

[07:12] Jonah: One more technical — do you support customer-run quantization profiles? We currently use int4 in some models in-house.
[07:20] Derek: We support quantized variants. For private deployment you can bring quantized model artifacts; for hosted/dedicated we provide verified quantized profiles. There are trade-offs with accuracy and cache behavior; we'll surface those in the cost/quality appendix.

[07:35] Maya: OK let's pivot to the proposal specifics so we can align on next steps. We'll propose two tracks: A) 12-month Dedicated commit for US + burst credits + EU region routing (hosted) B) 6-month EU private pilot + US Dedicated baseline. We'll put costs and timelines and the contract amendment draft.

[07:55] Priya: I think the product team prefers B to validate residency and then convert to full Dedicated for EU if pilot passes. Procurement might prefer A for predictability.

[08:05] Aisha: Right — procurement needs a clear PO schedule and acceptance criteria for the pilot. If the pilot meets p95 < 150ms and residency checks, we convert to full commit.

[08:15] Lena: We'll include pilot acceptance criteria: p95 threshold, KV cache hit rate target, and audit/log export validation.

[08:23] Marco: On monitoring — will we get token-level cost dashboards and traces? We need to map model keys to our product routes.

[08:30] Derek: Yes the Console exports token cost by API key/route, and you can add tracing hooks. We'll help map routes and create a cost-labsheet for your billing team.

[08:40] Priya: Another concern — latency in APAC. If we bring APAC regions later, what's typical latency from Tokyo to EU presence for failover?
[08:48] Derek: Cross-region failover is possible but will add network latency. Typical Tokyo->EU pings are 180–220ms, so you should avoid failover for latency-sensitive paths. We usually suggest regionally-local edges for APAC users.

[09:02] Jonah: Understood. We'll likely do EU for Europe and Tokyo for APAC in a later phase.

[09:08] Maya: Great. Let's confirm what we'll send after call: SOC2 report, private deployment diagram, draft amendment with two tracks, and the SE benchmark plan.

[09:18] Aisha: Thanks. Also remind us of the SLA targets for Dedicated (uptime & latency).

[09:23] Derek: Dedicated SLA: 99.95% uptime for serving runtime, latency SLOs we aim for p95 < 150ms for search-like workloads with Dedicated pool sized to 95th percentile. We'll annotate assumptions in the SLO.

[09:40] Priya: Okay I want one thing on the record — if we accept Dedicated, we want a scheduled monthly review with your CS team for cost and model performance.
[09:48] Lena: That's standard — we'll set monthly cadence for the first 6 months and then quarterly.

[09:55] Maya: Any other questions before we set dates?
[09:58] Priya: Not yet. We'll confirm internal timeline — procurement needs two weeks to finalize a PO after we review the amendment.

[10:06] Aisha: That's accurate. We'll aim to review by Dec 16.

[10:10] Maya: OK action recap: Derek runs the 1k qps benchmark, Maya sends amendment & pricing, Lena sends the onboarding diagram and SOC2, Priya/Aisha confirm residency and procurement timeline.

[10:22] Marco: Quick nit: when Derek shares logs, can we get the raw token-level traces to feed into our internal profiler?
[10:28] Derek: Yes, we can provide redacted logs with token-level detail. We'll coordinate secure transfer.

[10:35] Jonah: Also on model versions — we need version pinning for the pilot so we don't have any unexpected model upgrades during acceptance testing.

[10:42] Derek: Agreed — we'll pin the model version and freeze rollouts until the pilot acceptance window closes.

[10:48] Priya: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[10:50] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the docs.

[11:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: Auto-transcript had a few mis-hearings around 'KV cache' (appears as 'K V cash' in some exports) and 'KMS' was sometimes rendered as 'K M S'. Speaker labels were mostly accurate but occasional overlap between Jonah and Marco in the middle of the discussion.
